(Can we add an example for this sense?)

This entry needs quotations to illustrate usage. If you come across any interesting, durably archived quotes, then please add them!

Usage notes

[edit]

In Estonia and Latvia, it is often an underground place - e.g. a cave, cellar, fortress passage, well - but sometimes it is a place above ground, such as a gap in the wall of a building, a crack in a wall, a drill hole, etc.

Makasar

[edit]

Pronunciation

  • IPA(key): /ˈtana/, [ˈt̪ʰa.na]
  • Hyphenation: ta‧na

Etymology 1

[edit]

Inherited from Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *tanəq.

Noun

[edit]

tana (Lontara spelling ᨈᨊ)

  1. (archaic) land
  2. wet rice field; paddy
    Synonym: galung (Maros-Pangkep, Turatea, Bantaeng, Konjo)
Derived terms
[edit]
compounds
  • sewa tana
  • tana balang
  • tana bonto

Etymology 2

[edit]

Noun

[edit]

tana (Lontara spelling ᨈᨊ)

  1. unhusked rice grain (especially one accidentally left among husked rice)
    Jai dudu tananna
    There are still too many unhusked grains in the rice.
    Nipile tana berasaki
    He is picked out like an unhusked grain in the rice (idiomatic: to be rare or uncommon).
Derived terms
[edit]
compounds
  • tana berasaʼ

Etymology 3

[edit]

Noun

[edit]

tana (Lontara spelling ᨈᨊ)

  1. a species of tree (Trewia nudiflora), used as timber
    Synonym: tindo-tindo
Derived terms
[edit]
compounds
  • kayu tana

Māori

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

(This etymology is missing or incomplete. Please add to it, or discuss it at the Etymology scriptorium.)

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈtana/ [ˈtɐnɐ]

Determiner

[edit]

tana

  1. his, her of one thing

Usage notes

[edit]

A possessive determiner which must be followed by a noun, unlike tāna and tōna. This is the neutral or informal form and is not governed by the a and o categories. It cannot be stressed, in which case either tāna or tōna must be used, depending on the category of the noun.

Scottish Gaelic

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Old Irish tanae, from Proto-Celtic *tanawyos, from Proto-Indo-European *ténh₂us.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈt̪ʰanə/[1], /ˈt̪ʰana/[2]
  • (Barra) IPA(key): /ˈt̪ʰanʌ/[3]
  • (Sleat) IPA(key): /ˈt̪ʰænə/[1]

Adjective

[edit]

tana (comparative nas taine, superlative as taine)

  1. thin (not thick; not dense)
  2. shallow (water)
  3. thin, runny (liquid)
  4. flimsy (material)

[edit]

Tokelauan

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Proto-Polynesian *te-qa-na.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [ˈta.na]
  • Hyphenation: ta‧na

Determiner

[edit]

tana

  1. (alienable, definite) his, her
